content: {"rule": "K-C", "applies": "yes", "applies_why": "The judge adjudicates the D3 vs C6 collision, where the witnesses pressed against the defender's Isaiah 7:14 link are the challenger's own chain read together (the sign with its bounds, word-count rows, and mechanism rows), so this is exactly the chain-against-chain collision the rule governs.", "verdict": "BREACH", "quote": "the sign itself does not state the mechanism", "rule_words": "the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side", "room": "'never verse by verse' and 'the stating-verse test DG-61 retires': reading one, the judge's final clause decides the collision by the silence of the single sign-verse — what it does not state in its own words — so the verdict of UNDERDETERMINED rests on the retired test; reading two, the clause merely restates DR3's chain claim and the verdict rests on a footing comparison of the two chains. I weighed these: the judge names both chains but compares no footing, and the stated ground of the verdict is the sign's own non-statement, so reading one governs.", "why": "The judge resolved a chain-against-chain collision by what one verse itself fails to state in its own words — the very stating-verse test the rule retires at a judge's seat — instead of weighing the two chains' footing against each other."}
